newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian region blasts Moscow's tax collection plan.
newsitem.headline: Russian region blasts Moscow's tax collection plan.

text.p: The leader of Russia's autonomous region of Tatarstan said on Thursday that Moscow's campaign to boost tax collection was doomed and warned against taking it to the region without his consent, Interfax news agency said.
Interfax quoted Tatarstan president Mentimer Shaimiyev as saying Moscow's threats to use bankruptcies in a crusade against tax-dodging firms would not work.

"A feverish struggle for taxes and vain attempts to collect them remind us of the stagnation (the last years of the communist regime)," said Shaimiyev, who has won wide autonomy for his Volga river region.
"Now, as then, they are trying to get more milk from chronically undernourished cows."
President Boris Yeltsin, worried by endemic corporate tax dodging, this month set up an extraordinary commission to tackle the crisis.
Ministers this week named Tatarstan's KamAZ truckmaker as one of four big tax evaders and said it was in line for bankruptcy proceedings.
But Shaimiyev told Interfax that action taken without the agreement of his administration against Tatarstan-based firms were illegal and Moscow's orders would not be obeyed.
"Such decisions would contradict the treaty on separation of powers signed between Tatarstan and Russia," Shaimiyev said.
"Such actions of the federal centre will have no consequences in the republic."
